chunks: And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

"Indeed, Jibril عليه السلام dug with his foot five rivers, and the tongue of the water followed him: the Euphrates, the Tigris, the Nile of Egypt, the Mehran, and the river of Balkh. So whatever they irrigated, or was watered from them, belongs to the Imam, as does the ocean encompassing the world."

key_terms.الْبَحْرُ الْمُطِيفُ بِالدُّنْيَا: the ocean surrounding the world, also included in this ruling
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibril عليه السلام, the angel mentioned as causing the rivers to flow
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَنْهَارٍ: five rivers specially identified in the narration
key_terms.فَلِلْإِمَامِ: belongs to the Imam; indicating his entitled authority
key_terms.لِسَانُ الْمَاءِ: the flowing course or stream of the water that followed

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of the five rivers say about the Imam’s right over lands watered by them?
ai.summary: This hadith attributes the origin of five major rivers to Jibril عليه السلام and states that lands irrigated by them fall under the right of the Imam. In the chapter of khums, it indicates the Imam’s divinely sanctioned authority over certain natural resources and revenues.
